subject: science
question: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
rubric: States that magnesium reacts with air to form a protective oxide layer|2; Correct method of cleaning (sandpaper)|1; Correct reason — the ribbon then burns readily|2
model_answer: Magnesium reacts slowly with air to form a layer of magnesium oxide on its surface. This layer does not burn, so the ribbon is cleaned with sandpaper to expose the metal, which then burns readily in air with a dazzling white flame.
